item.text: The project is a minimal App Router page with no authentication or database. I’ll persist the preference in an HTTP-only cookie for this browser, render the current value server-side, and call `refresh()` from `next/cache` after toggling so the action stays on the current route.

The toggle is wired as a progressive-enhancement form on the server-rendered page. The cookie is the source of truth for the displayed state, and the action ends with `refresh()` without using a redirect. I’m reviewing the resulting diff now.

item.text:
Implemented the notification toggle on the Settings page.

- [app/actions.ts](/workspace/app/actions.ts) toggles the preference in an HTTP-only cookie, then calls `refresh()` from `next/cache` to update the current page without redirecting.
- [app/page.tsx](/workspace/app/page.tsx) reads the preference on the server and shows its current state and the button’s next action.

The preference defaults to on and is stored per browser because this project has no account or database layer. I reviewed the diff; I did not run tests or a build.
